headline: Discordia Server for People Whose Pets Look Disappointed in Them Hosts Intervention-Style Sessions
subheadline: Members share photos of judgmental animals and receive peer support
summary: A growing Discordia community helps members process the constant judgment emanating from their household companions.
content:
The Discordia server "Judged By Paws" has grown to 78,000 members who share a common experience: their pets look at them with visible disappointment, and they need to talk about it.

"My cat watches me eat cereal for dinner with this expression," wrote member @JudgedByWhiskers. "It's not neutral. It's assessment. She's calculating how far I've fallen. I posted a photo and 847 people confirmed: that's disappointment."

The server features channels organized by pet type (#cat-contempt, #dog-disapproval, #bird-side-eye) and by scenario (#judged-while-eating, #judged-for-sleep-schedule, #caught-talking-to-myself). The most active channel is #3am-shame-spiral, where members post real-time photos of pets witnessing their worst moments.

"I was eating shredded cheese directly from the bag at 2 AM," shared @WitnessedByMax. "My dog Max was just sitting there. Watching. Not begging. He didn't want any. He just wanted me to know he saw."

The community has developed a rating system for pet disappointment, from Level 1 (mild curiosity that could be judgment) to Level 5 ("active intervention energy"). Members vote on submitted photos, with heated debates over whether certain expressions constitute judgment or simply resting pet face.

"Some people post and their pet is clearly just sleepy," explained moderator @GuiltyAsCharged. "But others... you can see it in the eyes. The pet has opinions about their human's life choices. We validate that experience."

The server hosts weekly "intervention sessions" where members share their most judged moments and receive support. Common themes include being judged for screen time, food choices, and "what time I came home and in what condition."

Veterinarian Dr. Karen Walsh noted that while pets likely don't experience judgment as humans do, "the fact that people perceive it says something about our own relationship with self-assessment. The pet becomes a mirror."

"My goldfish looked disappointed in me yesterday," posted @EvenTheFishKnows. "A goldfish. With a three-second memory. And yet."

The server's motto: "They can't speak. But somehow they say so much."
author: Jennifer Park, Internet Culture Reporter
